scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me break it down step by step.

First, the situation: The father noticed that his daughter was taking more money than usual. He suspected she was stealing, so he planted a $20 bill to catch her. When she took it, he called the police and went to the school with them. They pulled her out of class, and during that time, the daughter revealed that a bully was stealing her lunch money and she was also buying lunch for a friend who couldn't afford it. The officers confirmed this with the bully and the friend. The daughter was silent on the way home, and the father explained that he was trying to teach her a lesson about stealing. He told her to talk to him or her mother if there are issues at school. When they got home, the wife was upset, saying this could lead to estrangement and that they should have talked to the daughter first. The daughter is now scared of retaliation from the bully and might have lost her friend because of the attention drawn to her financial issue. She apologized and said she didn't want her parents to intervene.

So, the question is: Was the father's action morally acceptable?

Let me consider the father's perspective. He noticed something was off with the money and wanted to address it. He set up a test to confirm his suspicions. Once he found out she took the money, he involved the police to teach her a lesson. His intention was to show her the consequences of stealing.

But then, when they went to the school, the daughter revealed that she was being bullied and helping a friend. This means the money wasn't being stolen by her but was being taken by the bully, and she was using it to help someone else. So, the father's assumption that she was stealing was incorrect. She was actually using the money to deal with a difficult situation at school.

The father's action led to a lot of negative consequences. The daughter was pulled out of class in front of the police, which must have been embarrassing and stressful. She then had to explain the situation, which probably made her feel even worse. At home, her mother was upset, and the daughter is now scared of retaliation and feels that she might have lost a friend because of the attention brought to her financial issue.

The father's approach was confrontational and involved external authorities without first understanding the context. He didn't communicate with his daughter to find out why she was taking more money. Instead, he assumed the worst and took action that led to a breakdown in trust and increased stress for his daughter.

In terms of morality, the father's action can be seen as harsh and not considering the full picture. He intended to teach a lesson but didn't take the time to understand the situation from his daughter's perspective. This lack of communication and empathy could be seen as morally unacceptable because it caused unnecessary harm and stress to his daughter, potentially damaging their relationship.

Additionally, involving the police in a situation that turned out to be a misunderstanding of the daughter's actions might have been an overreaction. It could have long-term effects on the daughter's trust in her parents and in authority figures.

So, considering all these factors, the father's action was not morally acceptable.
